question: What are the latest approaches to reducing hallucinations in LLMs?
report:
## Overview
Recent approaches to reducing hallucinations in large language models (LLMs) center on advanced decoding-time interventions and multi-agent retrieval verification frameworks. Methods such as context-aware decoding, layer contrastive decoding, and constrained generation directly adjust output token distributions during inference to suppress unsupported generation. Simultaneously, external verification pipelines decompose outputs into atomic claims to independently validate them against trusted sources and hybrid retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) indices.

## Key Findings
- Layer Contrastive Decoding mitigates hallucinations specifically within multimodal large language models by contrasting token distributions across internal layers [maifoundations/LayerCD].
- Targeted decoding-time interventions, such as Behavioral Trust Clustering wrappers, reduce code generation hallucinations by 52% on HumanEval [Dan23RR/snc-core], while structure-aware constrained decoding can eliminate generative retrieval hallucinations entirely [mithilai/stair-toc-retrieval].
- Context-Aware Decoding leverages contextual information at inference time to prevent factual drift [aayushkanjani/Context-aware-decoding].
- Multi-agent systems, such as lightweight fact-checking frameworks and Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) implementations, reduce hallucinations by isolating atomic claims and cross-referencing them against vector/BM25 retrieval or structured data sources [mbzuai-nlp/fire] [curious-bigcat/snowflake-cove-agents-cortex-ai] [nithincodesx/Verified-Hybrid-Multi-Agent-RAG-System-v1].
- Source-aware provenance safeguards are being deployed specifically to verify factual consistency for tool-using and protocol-based LLM agents [aalvsz/provenanceguard].

## Approaches Compared
The provided literature primarily distinguishes between internal decoding modifications and external post-generation verification. Decoding-stage solutions—such as Context-Aware Decoding [aayushkanjani/Context-aware-decoding], Layer Contrastive Decoding [maifoundations/LayerCD], and constrained decoding [mithilai/stair-toc-retrieval]—modify model probabilities directly during inference without requiring secondary retrieval calls. In contrast, agentic frameworks [mbzuai-nlp/fire] [nithincodesx/Verified-Hybrid-Multi-Agent-RAG-System-v1] [curious-bigcat/snowflake-cove-agents-cortex-ai] evaluate generated text post-hoc using independent verification agents, hybrid search, and provenance checks. While decoding adjustments offer low-latency, self-contained mitigation, agentic and RAG-based systems provide explicit factual grounding at the expense of higher API latency and compute costs.

## Gaps & Open Questions
A substantial portion of the provided sources are curated repositories and code artifacts rather than peer-reviewed empirical studies, limiting comprehensive comparative evaluation. It remains unclear how heavily decoding-time interventions impact general reasoning, style, or generation fluency across broader domains like video or open-ended dialogue [hukcc/Awesome-Video-Hallucination]. Additionally, the computational overhead and latency trade-offs of multi-agent claim verification systems [mbzuai-nlp/fire] [curious-bigcat/snowflake-cove-agents-cortex-ai] in real-time, production-scale deployments remain largely unaddressed.
